review_note: Abelian presheaf sheaf condition is equivalent to Čech degree-zero cohomology agreeing with F(U) for every covering. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$ of a site and an abelian presheaf $\mathcal F$, the degree-zero Čech group $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is the group of compatible families $(s_i)$, $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$, whose restrictions coincide on each fibre product $U_i\times_U U_j$. The natural map $\mathcal F(U)\to\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is restriction to the family.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian presheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$ and
\item for every covering $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
of the site $\mathcal{C}$ the natural map
$$
\mathcal{F}(U) \to \check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
(see Sites, Section \ref{sites-section-sheafification}) is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site and $\mathcal F$ is an abelian presheaf on it.
conclusions: The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf; (2) for every covering $\mathcal U$ of every object $U$, the restriction map $\mathcal F(U)\to\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is bijective.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-h0}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian presheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$ and
\item for every covering $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
of the site $\mathcal{C}$ the natural map
$$
\mathcal{F}(U) \to \check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
(see Sites, Section \ref{sites-section-sheafification}) is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
